Class AppleScrollBar.AppleBarUi

java.lang.Object
javax.swing.plaf.ComponentUI
javax.swing.plaf.ScrollBarUI
javax.swing.plaf.basic.BasicScrollBarUI
org.casserole.app.ui.ssh.AppleScrollBar.AppleBarUi
All Implemented Interfaces:
LayoutManager, SwingConstants
Enclosing class:
AppleScrollBar
private static final class AppleScrollBar.AppleBarUi extends BasicScrollBarUI
The AppleBarUi paints one floating bar. A press on the handle grabs that handle. A press on the track jumps the handle so the pointer is at its center. The buttons at the ends of the bar are hidden.

      public Dimension getPreferredSize(JComponent c)
      The getPreferredSize method reports a thickness only for a parent-laid bar. A null component returns zero width and zero height. A component whose client property casserole.apple.strip is not true returns zero width and zero height. A horizontal bar with that property returns zero width and a height of AppleScrollBar.BAR_PX. Any other component with that property returns a width of AppleScrollBar.BAR_PX and zero height.

    • seatThumb

      private void seatThumb(boolean vertical)
      The seatThumb method keeps the handle at AppleScrollBar.thumbSpan(int) and maps the value along the travel. A null bar returns immediately. A null track returns immediately. The track length is the track height for an upright bar. The track length is the track width for a bottom bar. The travel is the track length minus the handle length. The value minimum is the model minimum. The value maximum is the model maximum minus the extent. The handle starts at the track origin when the travel is not positive. The handle also starts at the track origin when the value maximum is not above the minimum. A positive travel with room in the model computes a fraction from the current value. A fraction below zero becomes zero. A fraction above one becomes one. The handle origin is the track origin plus that fraction times the travel, rounded to the nearest pixel. An upright handle is placed at x zero. Its width is the bar width, or one pixel when the bar width is smaller. Its height is the handle length. A bottom handle is placed at y zero. Its height is the bar height, or one pixel when the bar height is smaller. Its width is the handle length.
      Parameters:
      vertical - True for the upright bar.

    • paint

      public void paint(Graphics g, JComponent c)
      The paint method draws the track and the handle. A null bar returns immediately. A null graphics context returns immediately. The fade state comes from AppleScrollBar.motionOf(Component) on the bar. A missing fade treats the pointer as outside and the eased amount as zero. The bar is live while the pointer is on it or the button is down. The thickness moves from AppleScrollBar.THIN_PX toward AppleScrollBar.BAR_PX by the eased live amount. A live handle is fully opaque. A handle that is not live uses the eased inside amount times six tenths. A live track uses seven tenths opacity. A track with the pointer on the pane, and the bar not live, uses four tenths opacity. Any other track uses zero opacity. Zero handle opacity and zero track opacity return without drawing. The handle gray is 215 while the button is up and the pointer is off the handle. A pressed button uses gray 255. A thumb rollover, while the button is up, uses gray 245. The upright test uses the bar orientation. The left-to-right test uses the bar's component orientation. Antialiasing is turned on for the copy of the graphics context. An upright left-to-right bar draws from the right edge inward. An upright right-to-left bar draws from the left edge. The track uses AppleScrollBar.PLATE. The handle uses the chosen gray. A bottom bar draws from the bottom edge upward. That bottom bar does not consult the component orientation. The graphics copy is disposed.
      Overrides:
      paint in class BasicScrollBarUI
      Parameters:
      g - The graphics context.
      c - The bar component. This method paints from the scroll bar field.

    • tick

      void tick(float dt)
      The tick method advances this bar's thickness fade. The target is fully wide while the bar is hot or the button is down. The target is fully thin otherwise. AppleScrollBar.step(float, boolean, float) applies the elapsed time.
      Parameters:
      dt - The elapsed time, in seconds.

    • moving

      boolean moving()
      The moving method reports whether the thickness fade is still running. The end value is one while the bar is hot or the button is down. The end value is zero otherwise. The method returns true when the linear value is not that end.
      Returns:
      True while the thickness is still changing.

    • onPress

      private void onPress(MouseEvent e)
      The onPress method starts a drag or jumps the handle. A null bar returns immediately. A disabled bar returns immediately. A null event returns immediately. A button other than the left button returns immediately. The pressed flag and the hot flag are set. A press inside a handle with positive length stores the grab offset from the handle start. That press also marks the thumb rollover. Any other press centers the handle on the pointer and clamps it to the track. That jump clears the thumb rollover and calls moveThumb(int). The grab offset becomes the distance from the pointer to the jumped handle. The model is marked as adjusting. wake() starts the fade.
      Parameters:
      e - The mouse press.

    • onDrag

      private void onDrag(MouseEvent e)
      The onDrag method moves the handle by the stored grab offset. A null bar returns immediately. A null event returns immediately. A bar that is not adjusting returns immediately. A button other than the left button returns immediately. moveThumb(int) receives the pointer minus the grab offset. The thumb rollover follows whether the pointer is still inside the handle. wake() keeps the fade running.
      Parameters:
      e - The mouse drag.

    • onRelease

      private void onRelease(MouseEvent e)
      The onRelease method ends the drag. A live bar clears the adjusting flag. The pressed flag is cleared. A release outside the bar clears the hot flag and the thumb rollover. A null event leaves the hot flag as it was. A release inside the bar also leaves the hot flag as it was. wake() runs in every case that reaches it.
      Parameters:
      e - The mouse release, or null.

    • onMove

      private void onMove(MouseEvent e)
      The onMove method tracks the pointer on the bar. A null bar returns immediately. A null event returns immediately. The hot flag is set. The thumb rollover follows whether the pointer is inside the handle. wake() starts the fade.
      Parameters:
      e - The mouse move.

    • moveThumb

      private void moveThumb(int thumbPos)
      The moveThumb method moves the handle and writes the model value. The position is clamped to the track. An upright handle keeps its x, width, and height. A bottom handle keeps its y, width, and height. No travel sets the value to the model minimum and returns. A handle on the maximum end sets the value to the model maximum minus the extent and returns. Any other position maps the handle fraction across the value range. That value adds one half before the cast, so the fraction rounds to the nearest integer. The stored value is that integer plus the model minimum.
      Parameters:
      thumbPos - The requested handle start, in pixels.
